title: Type every referenced core object and specify Proposed Move Queue runtime semantics
desired_change: Add schemas and lifecycle contracts for Receipt, Authority, LogRecord, Eval, EvalRun, Gate, GateResult, OutcomeRecord, Capability, AgentSkill, Challenge, Comment, PoisonMarker, ForgettingAction, Release, and ResourceRef; define queue identity, deduplication, ordering, aging, retries, leases, concurrency, stale-write rejection, replay, dead-letter, and outcome closure.
expected_outcome: No prose-only core object or queue behavior requires Bryan to explain how it should serialize, validate, or behave under concurrency.

risk.rights_or_safety_impact: Untyped authority, evidence, and queue behavior can create silent mutation, duplicate execution, or unreconstructable decisions.

hidden_context_dependencies: The PR references many core objects but provides only four schemas.
The Proposed Move Queue is described as lanes and priorities without persistence, concurrency, or failure semantics.
Comment, challenge, decision, transition, receipt, and outcome boundaries are not machine-enforced.
No schema version compatibility or migration behavior exists for core object evolution.
acceptance_checks: Every normative object in the architecture has a schema and executable fixture.
Concurrent approvers cannot produce two operative outcomes for one versioned subject.
Comments cannot serialize as commands or transitions.
